question_text:
A plain carbon steel wire 3 mm in diameter is to offer a resistance of no more than $20 \Omega$. Using the data in  table 12.1 , compute the maximum wire length.

Reference:
"Table 12.1
Room-Temperature Electrical Conductivities for Nine Common Metals and Alloys
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|}
\hline Metal & Electrical Conductivity [ $(\Omega \cdot \boldsymbol{m})^{-1}$ ] \\
\hline Silver & $6.8 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline Copper & $6.0 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline Gold & $4.3 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline Aluminum & $3.8 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline Brass ( $70 \mathrm{Cu}-30 \mathrm{Zn}$ ) & $1.6 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline Iron & $1.0 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline Platinum & $0.94 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline Plain carbon steel & $0.6 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline Stainless steel & $0.2 \times 10^7$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}"The unit of the answer is m.
response:
The resistance of a wire is $R = \rho \dfrac{L}{A} = \dfrac{L}{\sigma A}$, so the maximum length is $L = R\,\sigma\,A$.

**Given data:**
- Diameter $d = 3\;\text{mm} = 3\times10^{-3}\;\text{m}$, so $A = \pi(d/2)^2 = \pi(1.5\times10^{-3})^2$
- $R_{\max} = 20\;\Omega$
- Plain carbon steel conductivity $\sigma = 0.6\times10^{7}\;(\Omega\cdot\text{m})^{-1}$

**Calculation:**

$$A = \pi(1.5\times10^{-3})^2 = 7.069\times10^{-6}\;\text{m}^2$$

$$L = R\,\sigma\,A = (20)(0.6\times10^{7})(7.069\times10^{-6}) \approx 848\;\text{m}$$

$$\boxed{848}$$
